events.title: The Bill of Rights becomes law
events.description: Virginia's ratification gave the first ten amendments to the U.S. Constitution the approval of the required three-fourths of the states. They took effect as the Bill of Rights.
events.significance: These amendments protect freedoms such as speech, religion, and fair trial. They remain the core of American civil liberties.

events.title: Sitting Bull is killed
events.description: The Lakota Sioux leader Sitting Bull was shot dead by Indian reservation police. It happened during an attempt to arrest him at the Standing Rock Reservation.
events.significance: His death raised tensions on the Plains. Two weeks later it was followed by the Wounded Knee Massacre.

events.title: The Twenty-first Amendment takes effect
events.description: The amendment was ratified on December 5. It took effect on December 15 and repealed the Eighteenth Amendment.
events.significance: Prohibition of alcohol in the United States ended after nearly 14 years. It is the only time a constitutional amendment has been repealed by another.

events.title: Gone with the Wind premieres
events.description: The film adaptation of Margaret Mitchell's Pulitzer Prize-winning novel premiered in Atlanta, Georgia.
events.significance: The film became a box-office phenomenon and won multiple Academy Awards. It remains a landmark of Hollywood history and is also criticized for its romanticized portrayal of the Old South.

events.title: The Boeing 787 Dreamliner makes its first flight
events.description: Boeing's new long-range airliner made its maiden flight from Everett, Washington.
events.significance: The 787 was among the first airliners built largely from composite materials, which made it more fuel-efficient. It changed long-haul air travel.
